Case: Yesenia is a 38-year-old who presents with 6 months of shoulder pain and progressive hand weakness. A steroid injection did relieve some of the pain, but she says this was short-lived and she feels that she is reaching a breaking point with the pain. During your physical exam, you note that she has some weakness on shoulder abduction and bilateral Hoffman's signs. Yesenia reveals that she was seen by a neurosurgeon two months ago, who informed Yesenia that her MRI showed a herniated disk at C4-5 causing neuroforaminal and canal stenosis. The neurosurgeon advised that Yesenia would need an anterior spine surgery, but Yesenia declined at that time. Repeat CT and MRi of the cervical spine confirm a disc herniation at C4-5 with slight progression in the canal stenosis.
Question: Would you offer hydrocodone to Yesenia? Yes or No? If yes, how much supply would you give – Low (1 week), or High (4 weeks) supply? Explain.
